title: Control-plane Eviction Shielding & SLO-priority Routing for Dedicated/Private
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: During multi-tenant Dedicated/Private upgrades and regional failovers we have observed control-plane churn causing broad tenant eviction cascades and SLO violations for latency-bound customers. Existing circuit breakers are per-service and fire too late for latency-sensitive routes. Goal: introduce an eviction-shielding layer in the control plane plus SLO-priority-aware routing so we can protect high-SLO tenants from noisy neighbor control-plane events and safely drain/upgrades with zero-regressions for P0-P1 customers. Scope: control-plane (replica manager, scheduler), API ingress routing, tenant score/prioritization, and rollback triggers. Out of scope: long-term autoscaling algorithm rewrite (separate ticket).
acceptance_criteria:
1) Tenant eviction events attributable to control-plane maintenance are reduced by >=90% for tenants flagged P0/P1 during staged upgrades in staging clusters.
2) Canary rollout mechanism can pin a region to SLO-priority routing for a tenant without manual network changes.
3) Automated circuit-breaker thresholds are adjustable per-tenant and per-route via config and respected by router within 100ms.
4) Runbook exists and tested in a tabletop exercise; post-mortem playbook validated with SRE.
5) No increase in token-level error rate for P0 customers during a simulated failover test (95th percentile).
plan:
Phase 1 (2 weeks): Design and telemetry - define tenant priority labels, SLO mappings, and new metrics (evictions_by_cause, control_plane_ltps). Create Confluence design doc and test harness.
Phase 2 (3 weeks): Implement eviction-shielding as an intercept layer in control-plane leader election and scheduler; add a tenant_score to allocation decisions. Add config flags for staging.
Phase 3 (2 weeks): Router work - SLO-priority-aware routing and per-tenant circuit-breaker parameters; integrate with routing policy service and rollout.
Phase 4 (1 week): Blue/green rollout in dedicated staging, run chaos tests (leader flaps, upgrade restarts), validate acceptance criteria, and ship.
Rollback plan: a single-day toggle to disable SLO-priority routing and revert scheduler changes. Detailed rollback in runbook link.
testing_plan: Unit + integration tests for scheduler decision logic; e2e scenario-driven chaos tests in staging (leader flaps, network partitions, staged upgrades); canary traffic with synthetic p99 latency checks; long-run soak for 48h after rollout. Test matrix documented in design doc.
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: misclassification of tenant priority could starve best-effort workloads. Mitigation: default fallthrough policy, quota windowing, and metrics to surface negative impact.
Risk: added router latency from priority checks. Mitigation: cache decisions, bounded lookup latency, and circuit-breaker fast-path.
Risk: config complexity during upgrades. Mitigation: feature-flagged rollout and staged enablement per-region.
